literal: He who cuts off the delusion called 'I' and 'mine' will enter a world exalted even to the heavenly beings.
translation: He who cuts off the delusion of 'I' and 'mine' will enter a realm that is higher than even the world of the heavenly beings.
modern: "நான்", "எனது" என்கின்ற அகந்தையை ஒழிப்பவன், தேவர்களுக்கும் மேலான உயர்ந்த உலகத்தை அடைவான்.
explanation: This couplet explains the ultimate reward of true renunciation. The poet identifies the root of all worldly attachment as the dual delusion of 'I' (egoism) and 'mine' (possessiveness), referred to here as 'cerukku' (delusion or pride). One who completely severs ('aṟuppāṉ') this deep-seated ignorance does not merely attain a temporary heaven. Instead, they enter a supreme state of liberation ('ulakam') that is far superior ('uyarnta') to the transient pleasures enjoyed even by the celestial beings ('vāṉōr').
